introduction: Explore the Savannah and the Pits through Mojo’s coconut recipes, the imp’s crafts, three alternative prybar trades and the golem’s four-badge vault key. The journal records accepted exchanges and explains optional preparation without inventing personal victories.
orientation: Mojo at the oasis crafts three separate coconut rewards. Each recipe has its own fruit quantities: large, small and broken coconuts are different ingredients, and a banana is different from a bushel. If you carry enough fruit for several recipes, Mojo can accept a different trade than you intended. Carry only the intended recipe’s complete ingredients loose before offering them; choosing a journal card does not select the trade.

The roaming nomadic merchant’s shop produces bananas and bushels of bananas, but purchases are currently unavailable while accounting is active. The journal cannot promise a new fruit supply from that shop. Supplied ingredients can fit a recipe without recording your own purchase or recovery.

SEARCH the appropriate ground, open palm tree, roc nest or anthill when needed to reveal hidden coconut ingredients, then take them out and carry them loose. Searching and finding are separate from the accepted recipe. Follow native container and visibility rules; a new day does not restock the world.

ASK CRAFTY about HELLO, KEY or GOODS in the imp’s quarters. The bone key uses the shorter leather strands from the vampire overseer, an eggshell among the gargoyle rocks and a femur hidden in the side nest. SEARCH hidden contents when needed. The key fits the secret slab toward the demon prince’s chamber.

The imp’s longbow uses the roc’s prepared remains and the longer leather strands from the same vampire. These strands look similar but cannot replace the shorter ones used for the key. A carried remains item is not evidence that you carved it or personally defeated the roc.

ASK FORTUNE about HELLO or TREASURE on the Savannah. Choose a single treasure trade: the flaming brazier in the demon prince’s vault, the overfiend’s gauntlets, or the Sultan of Snakes’ scepter. Each accepted exchange grants a prybar. The dialogue mentions treasure from two pits, but the actual exchanges accept one treasure each.

The prybar fits the hidden boulders beside the roc nest, opening the descent toward the Great Below. SEARCH hidden entrances, then use the relevant key and native OPEN/UNLOCK commands. The bone key and prybar are separate tools; shared open routes or a supplied tool do not prove who prepared the passage.

At the Great Below, gather the four different hidden badges: Hate from Spitelan, Pain from Gren, Fear from Gorgor and Rage from Scorn. SEARCH their contents or remains when needed and return all four loose to the granite golem for the vault key. One repeated badge cannot replace a missing different badge. The key fits the hidden vault below; a supplied badge does not prove your own captain victory.

ENTER the actual pit openings for their native destinations. The fiery portal from the Great Below leads to the Home of the Divine; another actual portal provides the return route. Portal travel, reading Nansuo’s scroll, captive-angel lore and outside trades remain separate outcomes.

The vault’s runestone follows separate epic rules. Room lore describes a rockworm loot route whose availability needs builder review. The masters cloak and revenant crown have their own equipment effects. Questions, worn gear and passive effects do not complete these recipes.

Ingredient rows show what you carry loose now; recorded exchanges remain after spending and recovery. Daily offers follow accepted exchanges, including each alternative prybar trade. Supplies follow the world’s reset rules. New discovery, encounters, journal, achievement and daily credit require active, ready accounting; frozen recovery is separate.
